claims.claim: Apollinaris the Younger was bishop of Laodicea in Syria and died around 382 AD.
He was a prominent fourth‑century theologian known for opposing Arianism and for the Christological doctrine later called Apollinarism.
The work titled *Fragments on Matthew* is a surviving portion of his biblical commentary on the Gospel of Matthew.
The fragments show he interpreted Matthew’s eschatological passages and argued against erroneous explanations offered by others.
Only fragments of the original commentary survive because his own writings were largely lost and are preserved mainly in later fifth‑ and sixth‑century polemical works.
More than 150 fragments of Apollinaris’ writings are extant, preserved chiefly in the works of Theodoret of Cyrrhus, Leontius of Byzantium, Emperor Justinian and other authors.
The fragments have been edited and published in modern scholarly editions, such as Hans Lietzmann’s *Schriften des Apollinaris*, making them accessible to contemporary researchers.

The fragments are important because they reveal the distinctive features of Apollinaris’ Christology and his exegetical method, shedding light on the theological controversies that led to his condemnation at the Council of Constantinople in 381.
